sections.heading: Where Practitioners Disagree & Alternative Playbooks
paragraphs: The first split is how money reaches the auction. NuView Trust lays out two live-auction routes: a checkbook-control LLC, or custodian-issued certified checks, such as four $5,000 checks against a $14,000 win, with the investor waiting weeks for the unused $1,000 to come back [Hqqt5H7mS3o @ 00:29:28]. For online sales NuView wants the bidding account fully funded upfront even when the county only asks for a 10% deposit. Next Generation runs the same paper route, issuing cashier's checks payable to the township, routing unused checks back into the IRA, and insisting every due diligence cost and dollar of income flow through the plan [l9-Us7KWWPM @ 00:58:36]. The CamaPlan speaker pushes the other way: bidding sites now demand a bank account, so they recommend setting up an entity with its own account instead of bidding under the custodian's FBO title alone [U08uLxrDVE4 @ 00:36:29]. Provident Trust lands in the same camp and flatly recommends a checkbook-control LLC for tax lien work [AcKbZeNuPr4 @ 00:56:15]. The trade-off is speed versus custody. Custodian checks keep every dollar inside the administrator's paperwork but lock capital in transit for weeks; the LLC gives the operator a live account that can pay a winning bid the same day.

The deepest rift is whether a lien is a yield instrument or a back door to the property. Ted Thomas plays both sides: they claim 97% pay off on paper, yet point to unpaid cases that delivered $200,000 properties for $1,000 to $2,000, and they flag divorce, fire, abandonment and death as signs a lien will not redeem [jDYlxXpw-e4 @ 00:32:14]. NuView Trust shuts that door hard, telling IRA investors not to buy a lien to get the property, because the best properties pay off fastest and the sweet spot is a good rate paid off late [Hqqt5H7mS3o @ 00:18:15]. Joanne Musa splits the difference by state selection: if the goal is acquiring real estate, move capital into tax-deed or redeemable-deed states rather than waiting out a lien [DHgFebJCtQU @ 00:21:29]. Chantelle Owens runs the acquisition playbook openly, reporting a personal redemption rate under one percent after a decade of buying only through tax sales in Georgia's redeemable-deed system [RDk1Gksh9R4 @ 00:59:37]. For portfolio construction this is a fork, not a nuance. A yield book is sized for volume, laddered reinvestment and fast redemption; an acquisition book is sized for fewer, larger positions with foreclosure, title and rehab capital held in reserve.

Practitioners also split on where a growing book should hunt. Ross Budrakey's rule is not to compete with banks and funds that dominate big counties, citing a $1 million fund in Fulton County paying above retail, and to target smaller counties in the path of progress instead [VmzztAnZ71w @ 00:09:40]. Kessler goes further on Florida, where banks bid everything down to a quarter of one percent and funds bid 0.025% on 50 liens per page, concluding it is not even worth participating anymore [vD0IitWLjZE @ 01:04:08]. The live-versus-online question cuts the opposite way depending on who is speaking. Joanne Musa prefers live sales precisely because online sales are more competitive [DHgFebJCtQU @ 00:13:05]. Ted Thomas agrees online auctions bid higher and in-person rooms push prices down, yet still calls online buyers the buyers of the future, since there are roughly 5,000 auctions across 3,000 counties, all of them online [jDYlxXpw-e4 @ 00:30:13]. The scaling playbook that falls out is geographic arbitrage: Kessler contrasts Maricopa at 1% to 2% with Apache County at 6% to 10%, and the operators who keep margins are the ones willing to travel to rooms and counties the institutions skip.

sections.heading: Firsthand Failure Modes, Traps & Economics Checks
paragraphs: The most expensive reversals come from skipping the property check, and several operators admit taking the hit themselves. Joanne Musa, who otherwise calls lien drive-bys a waste of gas, says they got burnt last year precisely by skipping inspection, and warns online photos can be one to three years old [DHgFebJCtQU @ 00:50:46]. On the Advanta IRA stage, Mo Hodges describes a buyer who paid $9,100 believing they had a Florida villa, received a strip of land instead, and is now in litigation, the textbook buyer-beware loss [c3YDDPR5wVo @ 00:38:35]. Kessler's first deed was a gutted mobile home that only broke even, which is why they now run two drive-bys, one by day and one by night, before any deed bid [vD0IitWLjZE @ 00:38:30]. The Tax Sale Support team puts the stakes bluntly: more people have lost money skipping on-site evaluation than by any other means, and they schedule visits a few days before the sale so redemptions clear first [sH-Esa2i1zE @ 00:26:28]. The economics check is simple. A $100 realtor visit or $15 photo set is trivial against a $9,100 strip of land, so the inspection budget belongs inside the per-deal cost before the bid ceiling is ever set.

The second trap is underpricing time and legal drag. Stephen Morel bought secondary-market liens after the redemption period had run, then hit an heir in occupancy with no probate opened and serial bankruptcy filings; expected time to liquidity of 9 to 18 months stretched to about three years and ended in cash-for-keys with first month's rent and moving costs paid [UyiZp8ocowM @ 00:29:16]. Morel also warns that one or two missed noticing deadlines can derail an entire year's returns [UyiZp8ocowM @ 00:39:08]. Ted Thomas tells buyers to plan on $2,000 to $5,000 extra for a clear title action, which normally takes months and in one case took 18 [jDYlxXpw-e4 @ 00:41:33]. In Georgia, Mo Hodges puts foreclosure at about 90 days after the 365-day period, with the investor paying for everything that happens after day 365 [c3YDDPR5wVo @ 00:42:21]. For a scaling portfolio these are not edge cases; they are recurring carrying costs that compound across every position held. A lien book funded with IRA dollars cannot pay a surprise attorney from outside the plan, so the legal reserve, the noticing calendar and a realistic three-year worst-case hold all have to be modeled before capital is committed.

Custody fees and rate compression are the quiet killers of a small IRA lien book. Next Generation's best structure is $325 per asset per year, on top of $100 per purchase and $5 per check or $30 per wire [l9-Us7KWWPM @ 00:16:30]. On a $1,000 to $2,000 lien bid down to single digits, a per-asset fee can consume most of the interest. NuView Trust prices differently, at $95 per purchase batch and $300 a year for all held liens, which favors buying many liens in one process [Hqqt5H7mS3o @ 00:36:44]. The same speaker reports winning Florida rates of 15% to 17% in 2008 now running below 6%. CamaPlan's math shows fees can still pencil out: a $15,000 account pays $390 in first-year fees and $1,193 over five years against $2,700 a year in interest, netting about 50% more than a taxable account [U08uLxrDVE4 @ 00:49:01]. Platinum Investment Properties Group explains why rates keep falling: Florida went online, hedge funds now bid a quarter of a percent to capture the 5% penalty, and sales went from 100 buyers to 50,000 [AcKbZeNuPr4 @ 00:59:40]. The check is mechanical: divide annual custody cost by expected interest per position before scaling the count.

callout.title: Before Capital Hits the Auction
callout.body: Every item below comes from a practitioner who paid for the lesson in time, legal fees, or lost principal; clear all four before scaling the position count.
items: Lock your exit strategy before you set your maximum bid, then execute at the auction without catching auction fever [Ross Budrakey — VmzztAnZ71w @ 00:36:42].

Have your REO offload channel proven long before buying liens in high-foreclosure states like Georgia and Texas, where REO rates run at least 60% [Platinum Investment Properties Group - Tax Liens — AcKbZeNuPr4 @ 00:21:38].
Calendar every noticing deadline with dated notices and proof of delivery, because one or two misses can derail a full year's returns [Kevin Bupp - Cash Flow Investor — UyiZp8ocowM @ 00:39:08].
Hand any foreclosure to a tax attorney and budget for every cost that lands after day 365, which the investor carries [Advanta IRA — c3YDDPR5wVo @ 00:44:29].

chapters.pull_quote: "The cost of one mistake greatly exceeds the cost of hiring a competent coach in the market you're interested in." — Ross Budrakey (VmzztAnZ71w @ 00:34:34).
action_checklist: Open the self-directed account in three moves: apply, fund it by rollover, transfer, or contribution, then invest [Advanta IRA — RDk1Gksh9R4 @ 00:06:36].

Form a checkbook-control LLC whose operating agreement names the IRA as owner, open the LLC's own bank account, and pay bids from it so interest flows back into it [Advanta IRA — c3YDDPR5wVo @ 00:06:23].

Run all lien certificates through one Wyoming LLC disregarded for federal tax, put each deed property in its own LLC, and assign a certificate to a second LLC before foreclosing [Clint Coons Esq. | Real Estate Asset Protection — bzu0eYCEXNg @ 00:02:10].
Pay subsequent taxes on your own liens to keep control of them and earn the statutory rate on those payments [CamaPlan Self Directed IRA — DHgFebJCtQU @ 00:39:42].
Raise other people's money through the LLC at 10% while the LLC earns Georgia's 20% penalty, refunding lenders if the bid strikes out [Ross Budrakey — VmzztAnZ71w @ 01:24:13].
Deploy steadily, buying about $200 a week to put $10,000 a year to work at 18%, and expect the compounding to show around years four and five [Personal Finance Tips — vD0IitWLjZE @ 01:05:56].
